text:
zoe.sales: Blocking POC for GreenLogistics (tenant: greenlogistics-poc). They did an Okta group push and Okta shows 204 but our tenant has zero users. Also the SAML test assertion shows NameID format unspecified and the NameID value looks like a session token. They want to run a short Dedicated throughput test and asked if we can provide a temporary hosted key while they fix provisioning. cc @harry.eng @mohit.se
harry.eng: two separate issues typically: 1) SAML NameID should be email or include an email attribute for login mapping; 2) SCIM requests must have correct auth token and Content-Type application/scim+json. Do we have their Okta SCIM example or raw request?
zoe.sales: customer pasted Okta logs: Okta shows SCIM push -> /scim/v2/Users returned 204. Okta admin included a raw request snippet where Content-Type is application/json and Authorization contains our onboarding API key (hosted_abc123). They admitted they used the onboarding key.
mohit.se: that explains a lot. Our SCIM endpoint expects two things: a SCIM service token (scim_*) in Authorization AND content-type application/scim+json. If Okta sends application/json some intermediaries or our parser could return 415 or ignore the body. Okta will still mark the push as success if the HTTP code is 2xx. Check our logs for 401/403/415/409.
paula.ops: looking at greenlogistics-poc SCIM logs now  I see a 415 Unsupported Media Type at 1912345742, followed by a 401 at 1912345790 (hosted key rejected for SCIM). The sequence fits: Okta got a 2xx initially (maybe our service returned 204 on a health route) but user creation failed.
scim-bot: SCIM webhook from okta.greenlogistics.example.com -> /scim/v2/Users returned 415 at 1912345742 (unsupported media type: application/json)
zoe.sales: customer thought the onboarding key they received for the hosted API would work for SCIM as well. They also asked if we can temporarily create a hosted API key scoped to the dedicated pool so they can run a 45-minute throughput test while they fix SCIM mapping.
harry.eng: we can create a short-lived inference key for the dedicated test but it will not authenticate SCIM. Action items for customer: 1) Change Okta SCIM connector bearer token to the SCIM service token we provide (scim_green_24h). 2) Set Okta provisioning "userName"/"externalId" to user.login or user.email to avoid duplicate/group id collisions. 3) Ensure Content-Type header is application/scim+json in the Okta provisioning connector advanced settings. Example curl they can run from their network to validate auth and content-type:
```bash
curl -i -X GET \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer SCIM_GREEN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" \
  https://scim.redwood-inference.example.com/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig
```
mohit.se: SAML fix: set NameID Format to urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:emailAddress or include an email attribute claim. Sample assertion for their Okta admin:
```xml
<saml:Assertion>
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:emailAddress">user@greenlogistics.com</saml:NameID>
  </saml:Subject>
  <saml:AttributeStatement>
    <saml:Attribute Name="email"><saml:AttributeValue>user@greenlogistics.com</saml:AttributeValue></saml:Attribute>
  </saml:AttributeStatement>
</saml:Assertion>
```
sec-bot: security reminder: for Private/VPC POCs we require SCIM traffic from allowed static IPs or mTLS per contract. For hosted trials a bearer scim token is okay but must be DM'd to the designated admin and rotated on expiry. Do NOT paste tokens in support screenshots. If the customer's proxy rewrites Content-Type or Authorization headers, they'll need a proxy rule to passthrough or to use mTLS.
paula.ops: I can issue two temporary creds: scim_green_24h (scoped to /scim only) and tmp_infer_green_45m (scoped to inference:generate, pool=dedicated-dl-1). Both will be limited to benchmark-lite model. Will that unblock the perf run?
zoe.sales: yes, that should work. Please add a note to rotate on expiry and PM me the secret via DM. Also I'm sending Okta mapping screenshots and asking them to change Content-Type and token.
scim-bot: SCIM webhook from okta.greenlogistics.example.com -> /scim/v2/Users returned 401 at 1912345790 (token invalid for SCIM endpoint)
paula.ops: created tokens: scim_green_24h (expires=1912432078), tmp_infer_green_45m (key_id=tmp_gl_45m, expires=1912348358, scopes=[inference:generate], pool=[dedicated-dl-1]). DM'ing secrets to Zoe now.
harry.eng: after they swap the token and set Content-Type properly, have them trigger a manual group push. If Okta still logs a 204 but users don't appear, ask them to capture the raw HTTP request/response (headers and body) from their side at the moment of push  that will show the actual Content-Type and Authorization values we received. Also check our SCIM logs for 201 user creation events.
zoe.sales: DM received, passing secrets to their admin via secure channel and sending the Content-Type + NameID instructions. I'll follow up when they re-run the push. Thanks team. Closing for now; will reopen if they need more help. :white_check_mark:
